title: Happy is the Man That Fears the Lord
program_note:
Happy is the Man that Fears the Lord is a setting of all of Psalm 112, based upon the traditional Russian Orthodox ‘intoning’ (or ‘reciting’) practice, whereby a cantor sings each line of text on a single tone, with a cadential formula at the end of each line.  The choir then responds with a cadential formula of its own.  Here, the piano provides the responses, but not always in the same ways.  Additionally, the piano provides reflections of the joy, fear, and anger of the text.  It is the second of the Two Russian Psalm Settings.

David S. Lefkowitz
6 March 2016
Los Angeles, CA
